description_full: Barratt Redrow plc engages in the housebuilding business in the United Kingdom. It also engages in the commercial development business, which includes offices, retail, leisure, industrial, and distribution properties under the Wilson Bowden Developments brand; and land development activities. In addition, the company manufactures timber frames under the Oregon Timber Frame brand; and furniture under the BD Living brand. It offers its homes under the Barratt Homes, David Wilson Homes, Redrow, and Barratt London brand names. The company was formerly known as Barratt Developments plc and changed its name to Barratt Redrow plc in October 2024. Barratt Redrow plc was founded in 1953 and is headquartered in Coalville, the United Kingdom.

financial_summary: BARRATT REDROW PLC is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $6.0B market cap on $8.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 4% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 14% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $565M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.79× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 5.0×.

Management returns a meaningful 7.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
